messages:
tara_support: Heads-up — ACME customer reported a sudden drop in embeddings vectors/sec around 15:03 PT. tokens/sec looks normal, but vec throughput fell ~6x and latency spiked. They see a mix of 200s and 401s then retries. Sharing initial logs + repro.
kira_sre: can you paste the request pattern and a log snippet? curious if we're seeing tiny batches after auth retries.
tara_support: here — customer call pattern: 300 req/s, batched client side = false. Model: open-embed-v2-384. sample curl:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-v2-384","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3"]}'
```
logs (excerpt):
```
2026-02-13T22:02:57Z auth: token validation failed: expired -> 401
2026-02-13T22:02:57Z gateway: retrying request (attempt=2)
2026-02-13T22:02:58Z embeddings-svc: request accepted -> queued (batch_size=1)
2026-02-13T22:02:58Z gpu-scheduler: dispatched batch_size=1 to gpu-02
2026-02-13T22:02:58Z embeddings-svc: success -> 200 (latency=340ms)
2026-02-13T22:02:58Z auth: token validated -> 200
2026-02-13T22:02:58Z embeddings-svc: request accepted -> queued (batch_size=1)
2026-02-13T22:02:59Z gpu-scheduler: dispatched batch_size=1 to gpu-02
2026-02-13T22:02:59Z embeddings-svc: success -> 200 (latency=330ms)
```
(note: many entries show batch_size=1 right after retries)
ben_ml: that pattern (401 -> retry -> single-item batches) will absolutely tank vectors/sec, tokens/sec stays stable when batching is client-side. Do we have a recent rollout touching auth token TTL or gateway retry behavior? Also check dims — customer payloads are consistent with model dim=384.
mike_infra: looking at infra metrics for that window: gpu-02 queue_len spiked with many single-item dispatches; utilization dropped to ~20% between 15:03-15:08. kernel latencies were normal but throughput small batches -> poor GPU packing. Also saw an auth-service spike in error rate at 15:02:59 (token-exchange latency increased).
ops-bot: alert #auth-service error-rate > 5% at 2026-02-13T22:02:57Z :warning:
kira_sre: remediation steps proposed:
- ask ACME to enable client-side batching (or our SDK batching) as a stopgap
- increase gateway retry backoff and coalesce retries per user/token to avoid immediate single retry floods
- short-term: configure embeddings route to buffer small requests into 50ms batch window for that customer (can be targeted by route override)
- long-term: fix auth token rotation race — we think token TTL/rotate process returned occasional 401s for live tokens
tara_support: I passed those to customer. they prefer server-side mitigation while they patch their client. can infra toggle the route buffer for acme-prod? also want repro steps so we can confirm fix.
mike_infra: I can flip a transient per-customer batch window (route override) — doing it now (will throttle to 50ms, max_batch=128). will monitor gpu queue and vec/sec.
ben_ml: quick repro we used locally:
1) run a script that sends 200 req/s with Authorization header that randomly fails 5% of requests (simulate token rotation)
2) run with client batching disabled -> observe vectors/sec drop 5-7x
3) enable server batching window 50ms -> vectors/sec recovers ~4.5x
script gist (pseudo):
```python
for i in range(1000):
  if random()<0.05: return 401 then retry immediately
  send_request(payload)
```
kira_sre: action items:
- mike_infra: enable route buffer for acme-prod now and monitor for 30m (assigned)
- infra: correlate auth-service deploys around 15:00 (assigned to infra oncall)
- devex: document recommended SDK retry/backoff best-practices and default client-side batching config
- support: keep customer updated; collect samples of Authorization header rotation cadence
tara_support: ack. will patch customer note + ask for token rotation schedule. assigning follow-ups.
mike_infra: route override applied at 22:05Z. initial metrics show gpu_queue_len smoothed and vec/sec trending up. will post follow-up in 15m. :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: deployment-note: route-override applied by mike_infra (change-id=chg_89231)"
